# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — prompt: make solution code GENERALIZE across the hidden multi-input grading (+ data_only for formulas, answer_position semantics)
- Changes I made (all in `prompt.md`, additive knowledge, no decision rule loosened):
  1. New top section "How you are graded": the final code is re-run on SEVERAL hidden input files of differing size/values/control-cell choices → size loops from live data (`ws.max_row`), read control cells live, match lookup keys, never hardcode answers or dims from `answer_position`/preview. (cluster: 52216, 418-29, 160-6, 53161 flakiness)
  2. `answer_position` = graded OUTPUT window, NOT the source extent / operating window; for delete-blank-rows/shift tasks operate on the WHOLE sheet (`ws.delete_rows`) so outside rows flow in. (cluster: 160-6, 347-49)
  3. Read formula-cell results with `load_workbook(path, data_only=True)`; default returns formula TEXT and breaks aggregation. (cluster: 374-9, deterministic 0.00)
  4. Coordinate clarity: absolute A1 coords + worked `E2:H5`→rows2-5/cols5-8, openpyxl exact-cell targeting, pandas header/index + `to_excel` drops-other-sheets caveat; inspect-first; read-back verify before finishing.
  - Kept all six original constraints (Cell/Sheet modify-only, prefer literals, save+mkdir, read-carefully, error→fix).
- Expected effect + why safe: fixes the [1,0,0]/[1,1,0] "passes visible, fails hidden" pattern (418-29, 52216) and the mis-scoped delete/shift (160-6), and the formula-string bug (374-9). SAFE: passing 47484 already reads dynamically (no formulas, single-sheet); passing 40467 is Cell-Level D1:D10 fixed-size writing formulas it doesn't read back — none of the four rules change their trajectory. Verified `data_only` returns formula text locally; verified E2:H5 col indices.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none exist (seed). No regressing edit to avoid yet.
- Refuted hypotheses: "openpyxl-vs-pandas mechanics is the root cause" — REFUTED by subagent evidence (47484 passes on pure pandas; 418-29's failing trial uses openpyxl). Do not spend a future iteration forcing openpyxl as the fix.
- High-value clusters NOT cracked: 32468 (rolling 12-vs-13-month window off-by-one — pure arithmetic interpretation; needs graded expected values, would overfit to special-case). 55457 (instruction field is genuinely EMPTY — data defect, unfixable by prompt).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this is rejected, the lever to try next is per-cluster worked micro-examples (e.g. one concrete blank-row delete_rows example) rather than more general prose.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, attack 32468's window boundary with a precise instruction-parsing rule; re-examine whether 347-49's blank-row/label-row detection needs a sharper "whole-row emptiness across the used range" rule.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.473 Δ=+0.007 · fixed={160-6, 418-29} · broke={—}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.

<!-- cap-evolve:journal-append-below — add your Iteration entry under this line; do not edit anything above it -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — re-ship cand_0001's safe edits, SHARPEN them with worked examples, and ADD the "write an Excel formula" lever for Excel-native tasks
- Changes I made (all in `prompt.md`, additive knowledge / narrowing only; no decision rule loosened):
  1. Sharpened §"How you are graded" with a WRONG-vs-RIGHT worked example: `region='Metro'` (or scanning for whichever appears) is WRONG; `region = ws_inputs['A14'].value` + match source rows by (region,label) is RIGHT. (cluster: 52216, 418-29, 53161 — hardcoded selectors)
  2. Kept `data_only=True` formula-reading with a concrete sum-of-formula-cells worked example. (cluster: 374-9 and the general SUM-of-formulas class)
  3. NEW paragraph in §"Producing and checking the output": the output workbook is recalculated by LibreOffice before grading, so writing the correct Excel FORMULA (SUMIFS/COUNTIFS/INDEX-MATCH/EOMONTH/cross-sheet) is equally valid and often MORE reliable than an off-by-one Python reimplementation. Kept "prefer literals when you can compute exactly" as the first choice. (cluster: 32468, 53161)
  4. Kept whole-sheet `ws.delete_rows` rule (cluster 160-6) and `answer_position`=graded-output-window + A1 coordinate worked example (cluster 418-29), both cand_0001-confirmed fixes.
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  1–2. Fix the [1,0,0]/[1,1,0] "passes visible input, fails hidden variants" pattern by forcing live reads + key matching. SAFE: passing 47484 already reads dynamically (no selector, 0 source formulas); passing 40467 has no selector and doesn't read source — neither trajectory changes.
  3. Give 32468/53161 a reliable path (emit the Excel function instead of reimplementing it). SAFE and GROUNDED: 40467 currently PASSES by writing a formula → LibreOffice recalc is provably active in scoring; and BOTH passing tasks' golds are themselves formulas that recalc correctly, so even full adoption of the formula path keeps them passing. Literals stay the first-choice, so it's additive not a behavior flip.
  4. Framework already confirmed these FIXED 160-6/418-29 with no breakage.
- Building on prior RESULTS: cand_0001 RESULT = REJECTED on significance (Δ=+0.007) but fixed={160-6,418-29} broke={}. Its whole batch was reverted, so I RE-INTRODUCE every one of its edits (all were non-breaking) and ADD more fix surface (formula lever + sharper examples) to clear the significance bar. I did NOT drop any cand_0001 edit because none regressed a task.
- Refuted hypotheses (do not re-test): "openpyxl-vs-pandas mechanics is the root cause" — REFUTED (47484 passes on pure pandas; 418-29's failing trial used openpyxl). Do not force openpyxl as the fix.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 32468 (rolling 12-vs-13-month boundary) — Python EOMONTH+11 matched only 19/31 rows; I'm attacking it INDIRECTLY via the write-the-formula lever rather than a special-case parser (which would overfit). 374-9 inputs 2/3 (answer = exactly 2×naive-sum, each state once) — unreconciled data anomaly, left as partial.
- Plateau signal: only one prior RESULT (flat/rejected-on-significance, not on regression). Lever switch this iteration = add a NEW capability path (write Excel formulas, leaning on the recalc step) + convert general prose into concrete worked examples, since cand_0001 showed the general prose alone moved the score only slightly.
- Focus next iteration: if this clears the bar, verify 32468/53161 actually flipped via the formula path in the new trajectories; if a formula-path task still fails, check whether LibreOffice recalc leaves a `None` cached value for that function (would need a compute-then-write fallback). Re-examine 347-49 blank-row/label detection only if its gold turns out consistent.
